_comment: One TTFV receipt per reader per track. Fill by hand following docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md; delete no keys. Null means not reached, not applicable, or unknown. Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

reader._comment: handle: a public handle, no other personal data. kind: cold | maintainer | ai-agent; only cold receipts without coaching events count toward cold-reader metrics.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.
project.description: examples/recipes/python_agent copied to a temporary directory, arci.yaml removed; project dir <tmp>

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.interpretation_answer: INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2): with only 8 smoke trials per arm and no injected fault, both arms went 8/8, but the bounds on the difference [-0.42, 0.42] cross the -0.10 margin, so there is not enough evidence either way; no regression is claimed and CI would stay non-green. The tool told me this was the expected smoke result and that I should pick a confirmatory N with `arci plan` (and, I think, add a fault like --fault tool_timeout:reserve) before running a real experiment.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

coaching_events.what: Before readme_opened (not stamped): the facilitator prompt stated that this harness blocks `uv tool install` and that uvx or a uv venv are alternatives; it also prescribed the timestamping wrapper and the milestone names. No explanation of ARCI was given.

notes: Install method: uv venv .venv + uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci (installed agent-reliability-ci==0.8.0 from PyPI; venv picked CPython 3.13.12), then .venv/bin/arci. README's `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` was denied by the harness.. Commands: P=$(mktemp -d); cp -R examples/recipes/python_agent/. $P/; rm $P/arci.yaml ; uv tool install agent-reliability-ci   (denied by harness, never executed) ; uv venv .venv ; uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci ; .venv/bin/arci --help ; .venv/bin/arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed   (failed, exit 3) ; .venv/bin/arci init checkout-retry --baseline app.v1:run --candidate app.v2:run --toolset tests.world:make_world --oracle tests.world:passed --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}'   (exit 0) ; cat arci.yaml ; .venv/bin/arci run arci.yaml   (exit 2) ; ls runs; ls runs/checkout-retry ; shasum -a 256 runs/checkout-retry/decision.json ; .venv/bin/arci gate runs/checkout-retry   (exit 2) ; shasum -a 256 runs/checkout-retry/decision.json. Store: <tmp> with decision.json, events.jsonl, manifest.json, trials.jsonl; gate line: VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2). scaffold_start is null: the reader's stamp was taken at the failed first `arci init` (2026-10-13T12:11:25Z), and the successful second invocation was not stamped, so the scaffold duration is unknown. readme_opened is the Track A stamp (one README read for both tracks). store_validated stamp and the protocol 4.4 total are null (the reader validated the store itself; the facilitator did not stamp it). agent_execution summed from the store's trials.jsonl by the builder. AI-agent reader (Claude opus via the Workflow tool, persona: an ML engineer who builds LLM agents with tool calls and evaluates them with ad-hoc scripts); self-stamped milestones with `date -u` under the facilitator's wrapper; machine shared with the orchestrator session (not controlled). Never counted as a cold reader. Protocol 2.1 deviation: the maintainer checkout was present on the machine; the reader read README.md from it and Track B copied the sample tree from it (no clone was made by the reader). Files read: README.md, <tmp> (generated by arci init), directory listing only of the copied sample project (app/__init__.py, v1.py, v2.py, tests/__init__.py, world.py, README.md were not opened). Confusions: The README's 'Gate your own agent' commands do not mention --task, but the sample toolset needs a task with order_id; init failed with KeyError: 'order_id' until I guessed --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' from the hand-written YAML example. A first-timer would not know which task keys their own toolset expects to be required here. | The README one-liner chains `uv tool install ... && arci init ... && arci run ...`, which assumes arci lands on PATH; with any other install route (venv) I had to call .venv/bin/arci. | Without --fault the scaffold runs a 'clean' condition only, so the run did not actually exercise v1 vs v2 under the retry-relevant fault; both arms were 8/8. It was unclear from the README whether I was supposed to add --fault tool_timeout:reserve for the 'checkout-retry' example; I followed the commands as written. | The README is long and dense (Jev decision endpoint, calibration audit, evalopt independence) before reaching 'Gate your own agent'; the part I needed was near the bottom. | Track A wrapper uses ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, which is empty under zsh (this machine's shell), so the first demo run printed 'exit: ' with no code; I re-ran the demo under bash to get the exit code. | The venv was created with CPython 3.13.12 although the task said 3.14 is on PATH; uv picked it on its own. Not a problem, just unexpected.. Reader notes: Timings: demo 12:09:52Z -> 12:11:05Z (~73 s, including uvx env resolution; first output after ~1 s, so the package was apparently already cached); rerun 75 s. Own-agent path: install 1 s (packages resolved from uv cache in 1 ms, so this is not a cold-network install), scaffold 6 s including one failure and retry, run 2 s. Total README-open to own verdict ~107 s. Demo counts matched recorded run (A 192/200, B 132/200, A-vs-A 192/200, C PASS). Decision.json sha256 unchanged after `arci gate`, and gate reproduced INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2). Machine state: load average 8.46 / 5.99 / 3.79 at 12:12:59Z, consistent with other agents running in parallel; no lingering arci/pytest processes found by ps at that moment. The uv cache was warm (installs took milliseconds), so install timing is not representative of a true first visitor. I did not open any docs/ file, the sample project's own README, or its source files; I did not read the generated store files beyond listing and hashing. I did not run arci plan or add a fault, so my own run says nothing about v1 vs v2 under a timeout.

failures.what: `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` was blocked by the harness: "Permission to use Bash with command cd <tmp>; date -u ...; uv tool install agent-reliability-ci; ... has been denied." (timestamp taken right after the denial; the denied command's own date never ran). Chose route: uv venv .venv + uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python agent-reliability-ci, then .venv/bin/arci.

First arci init (exit 3): "error: CliError: init: --toolset tests.world:make_world: calling it with the task and seed 0 raised KeyError: 'order_id'; check the toolset factory and --task". Fixed by adding --task '{"order_id": "order-7"}' (second attempt exit 0 at 2026-10-13T12:11:31Z).
